title: Habibi Takes the Throne: Kaushal Wins Buckaroo Bowl I as the League Is Born
dek: In the Buckaroo Football League's first season, the Habibsters went wire to wire as the top seed, Team Pillbert played the villain all the way to the final, and Ben Dover found the basement through the consolation ladder.
body: Every dynasty needs a first chapter, and the Buckaroo Football League wrote its own in 2023. Six friends, one ESPN league, and zero trades all season. That last number tells you everything about the league's opening-year trust levels. Nobody blinked, nobody dealt, and when the dust settled, Kaushal was holding the first trophy in league history.

The Habibsters were the class of the regular season, going 10-4 and scoring 1,528.8 points to lock up the No. 1 seed. Kaushal treated the schedule like a Georgia highway with no trooper in sight: foot down, no brakes, see you at the finish line. Right behind him was Alan's Team Pillbert at 9-5 with 1,499.3 points. Philly also posted the highest single week of the season, a 156.18 haymaker in Week 3 that announced early that the league's villain had arrived and brought receipts.

The real heartbreak of 2023 belonged to Mekhi. Kai's Dawgs led the entire league in points with 1,542.8, more than the champion, and somehow finished 6-8. That's the fantasy equivalent of outgaining your opponent by 200 yards and losing on a doink. Randy's The fumblers went the other way, squeezing a tidy 7-7 record out of 1,462.9 points to grab the third seed. And with zero trades on the books, Randy can at least say his roster stayed exactly as stubborn as he is.

The playoffs ran on two-week totals, and the top seeds held serve. Kaushal dispatched Mekhi 237.54 to 196.12, ending the Dawgs' points-machine season with a reminder that fantasy football doesn't hand out trophies for style. On the other side, Alan outlasted Randy 234.86 to 216.44, sending the bad guy into the first-ever Buckaroo Bowl. The fumblers finished third and the Dawgs fourth, which, for the team that scored the most points, is a sentence Kai will be thinking about for a while.

Buckaroo Bowl I was supposed to be a heavyweight fight between the top two seeds. It turned into a coronation. The Habibsters rolled Team Pillbert 251.36 to 192.08 over two weeks, a 59-point margin that left no room for controversy. Habibi became the league's first champion, and the villain's arc ended the way the good movies do: close enough to taste it, then flattened in the final act.

Down at the bottom, things got weird. Ramon's Araleasers went 4-10 with a league-low 1,375.3 points and took the season's ugliest week, a 65.9 in Week 9. Still, Brucie escaped the cellar. The consolation ladder dropped Sonny's Ben Dover to sixth despite a 6-8 record and the fifth seed, which means the commissioner built a league and then finished last in it. In hindsight, it was the opening scene of one of the great redemption arcs in league history, but in 2023 it was just a man staring at a ladder he climbed the wrong way.

So the first book closes with Kaushal on top, Alan one step short, Mekhi wondering what more he could have possibly done, and Sonny with a front-row seat to everyone else's celebration. Six teams, one champion, and zero trades. The Buckaroo Football League was officially open for business, and Habibi set the bar.
